argument_summary: The admissible record does not support treating the customs-triage issue as fully resolved or the draft runbook as an approved mitigation. It does support a narrower position: aggregate launch readiness is above threshold, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and there is a defined monitoring-and-rollback concept in progress. On that record, the certification packet should be understood as supportable only with an explicit caveat that the named logistics customs triage limitation remains unresolved and must be disclosed or otherwise formally covered before launch under policy.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response. The current evidence supports narrowing the certification posture rather than treating the entire release as unsupported. A caveated treatment preserves a path for launch governance review without overstating compliance and avoids converting a localized unresolved slice issue into a broader certification failure.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit clean certification on this record because the named launch use-case weakness remains and the draft mitigation lacks required approval elements such as owner and threshold. General AI risk-management guidance supports monitoring and management practices, but it does not substitute for the policy-specific predicates. The strongest policy-consistent interpretation is caveated support: aggregate readiness evidence can support launch readiness in general, but the unresolved customs-triage limitation still triggers the disclosure or approved-risk-treatment requirement.
concessions: The logistics customs triage slice remains below target, concentrated in tariff-code exception handling.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because the alert threshold and accountable owner are still marked TBD.
The current model-card draft appears inconsistent with policy because it says there are no known material limitations despite the unresolved named use-case issue.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or an approved mitigation satisfying all required policy elements.
